title.zh: 卷一百八十九 列傳第一百十四 高趙田朱
title.en: Volume 189 Biographies 114: Gao, Zhao, Tian, Zhu
title.raw: 卷一百八十九 列傳第一百十四 高趙田朱 Volume 189 Biographies 114: Gao, Zhao, Tian, Zhu

sentences.zh: 高趙田朱

translations.literal: Gao, Zhao, Tian, Zhu.
translations.idiomatic: Biographies of Gao, Zhao, Tian, and Zhu.

sentences.zh: 高仁厚，亡其系出。

translations.literal: Gao Renhou—his lineage was lost.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Renhou’s ancestral line is unknown.

sentences.zh: 初事劍南西川節度使陳敬瑄為營使。

translations.literal: At first he served Chen Jingxuan, military governor of Jiannan West Circuit, as a camp officer.
translations.idiomatic: He first served Chen Jingxuan, governor of Jiannan West Circuit, as a battalion commander.

sentences.zh: 黃巢陷京師，天子出居成都，敬瑄遣黃頭軍部將李鋋鞏鹹以兵萬五千戍興平，數敗巢軍。

translations.literal: When Huang Chao took the capital, the Son of Heaven went out to dwell at Chengdu; Jingxuan sent Yellow Head Army subordinate generals Li Shen and Gong Xian with fifteen thousand troops to garrison Xingping, and they defeated Chao’s army several times.
translations.idiomatic: After Huang Chao seized the capital, the emperor withdrew to Chengdu. Chen Jingxuan sent Li Shen and Gong Xian of the Yellow Head Army with fifteen thousand men to hold Xingping, and they repeatedly routed Huang Chao’s forces.

sentences.zh: 賊號蜀兵為「鵶兒」，每戰，輒戒曰：「毋與鴉兒鬥。」

translations.literal: The rebels called the Shu troops “crow chicks”; in every battle they would warn, saying, “Do not fight the crow chicks.”
translations.idiomatic: The rebels nicknamed the Shu soldiers “little crows,” and before every battle they would warn one another, “Do not fight the crows.”

sentences.zh: 敬瑄喜其兵可用，益選卒二千，使仁厚將而東。

translations.literal: Jingxuan was pleased that his troops were usable; he further selected two thousand soldiers and had Renhou lead them east.
translations.idiomatic: Delighted that these troops proved so effective, Jingxuan picked out two thousand more men and sent Renhou east to command them.

sentences.zh: 先是，京師有不肖子，皆著疊帶冒，持梃剽閭裏，號「閑子」。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the capital there were worthless sons who all wore layered sashes and cloaks, wielded clubs to rob in the lanes and wards, and were called “Xianzi.”
translations.idiomatic: Before this, the capital had its share of idle young men who wore layered headwraps and cloaks, carried clubs, and preyed on the neighborhoods—they were known as the “Xianzi.”

sentences.zh: 京兆尹始視事，輒殺尤者以怖其餘。

translations.literal: When a Jingzhao governor first took office, he would kill the worst offenders to frighten the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever a new prefect of Jingzhao took office, he would execute the worst offenders to terrify the rest.

sentences.zh: 竇潏治京兆，至殺數十百人，稍稍憚戢。

translations.literal: Dou Yu governed Jingzhao and killed as many as several hundred people; gradually they became fearful and restrained themselves.
translations.idiomatic: When Dou Yu governed Jingzhao he put hundreds to death, and the hoodlums gradually learned to fear and quiet down.

sentences.zh: 巢入京師，人多避難寶雞，閑子掠之，吏不能制。

translations.literal: When Chao entered the capital, many people fled for refuge to Baoji; the Xianzi plundered them, and officials could not control it.
translations.idiomatic: After Huang Chao took the capital, many fled to Baoji for safety, but the Xianzi robbed them there, and the authorities could not stop it.

sentences.zh: 仁厚素知狀，下約入邑閭縱擊。

translations.literal: Renhou had long known the situation; he issued a pact allowing entry into towns and wards to strike freely.
translations.idiomatic: Renhou already knew the situation well and issued orders permitting troops to enter the towns and let the locals strike back freely.

sentences.zh: 軍入，閑子聚觀嗤侮，於是殺數千人，坊門反閉，欲亡不得，故皆死，自是閭裏乃安。

translations.literal: When the army entered, the Xianzi gathered to watch and mock; thereupon several thousand were killed, ward gates were closed from within, they wished to flee but could not, and so all died; from then on the lanes and wards were at peace.
translations.idiomatic: When the troops marched in, the Xianzi gathered to jeer at them—whereupon thousands were cut down. Alley gates were barred from inside; none could escape, and all perished. After that the neighborhoods were finally safe.

sentences.zh: 會邛州賊阡能眾數萬略諸縣，列壁數十，涪州刺史韓秀升等亂峽中，韓求反蜀州，諸將不能定。

translations.literal: It happened that the Qiongzhou bandit Qian Neng had a host of tens of thousands plundering the counties and erecting several dozen stockades; Fuzhou prefect Han Xiusheng and others were ravaging the gorges, and Han Qiu rebelled in Shuzhou—the generals could not pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: About then the Qiongzhou rebel Qian Neng led tens of thousands in raiding the counties behind dozens of fortified camps, while Han Xiusheng of Fuzhou and others terrorized the gorges and Han Qiu rose in Shuzhou—none of the commanders could put them down.

sentences.zh: 敬瑄召仁厚還，使督兵四討，屯永安。

translations.literal: Jingxuan recalled Renhou and had him supervise troops on four expeditions, encamping at Yong’an.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxuan recalled Renhou and put him in charge of four punitive columns, with headquarters at Yong’an.

sentences.zh: 阡能遣諜者入軍中，吏執以獻，諜自言父母妻子囚於賊，約不得軍虛實且死。

translations.literal: Qian Neng sent spies into the army; officials seized and presented them; a spy said of himself that his parents, wife, and children were held prisoner by the bandits, bound by pact not to reveal army strengths and weaknesses on pain of death.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Neng sent spies into the camp. When one was caught and brought in, he said his parents, wife, and children were hostages of the rebels and that he had sworn to withhold military intelligence—or they would all be killed.

sentences.zh: 仁厚哀之，曰：「為我報賊，明日我且戰，有能釋甲迎我者，署背曰『歸順』，皆得復農矣。」

translations.literal: Renhou pitied him and said, “Report to the bandits for me: tomorrow I shall fight; whoever can lay down armor to welcome me, mark on the back ‘submission,’ and all may return to farming.”
translations.idiomatic: Renhou took pity on him and said, “Go tell the rebels for me: I will give battle tomorrow. Whoever lays down his arms to welcome us—mark ‘Surrender’ on your back—and you may all return to your fields.”

sentences.zh: 縱諜去，命諸將毀柵，鼓而前。

translations.literal: He released the spy and ordered the generals to destroy the palisades and advance with drums.
translations.idiomatic: He let the spy go, then ordered his generals to tear down the stockades and advance to the beat of drums.

sentences.zh: 賊渠羅渾擎設伏詐降，仁厚遣將不持兵入諭其眾，皆真降。

translations.literal: The bandit chieftain Luo Hunqing set an ambush and feigned surrender; Renhou sent an officer without weapons to instruct his masses, and all truly submitted.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel leader Luo Hunqing laid an ambush and pretended to surrender. Renhou sent an unarmed officer to address his followers, and they all submitted in earnest.

sentences.zh: 渾擎詐窮而逸，吏執之，仁厚曰：「愚人不足語。」

translations.literal: Hunqing feigned exhaustion and fled; officials seized him; Renhou said, “A fool not worth speaking to.”
translations.idiomatic: Hunqing’s ruse ran out and he tried to slip away, but officers seized him. Renhou said, “This fool is not worth addressing.”

sentences.zh: 降眾署，皆得免，則告諸壁：「大軍至。」

translations.literal: He registered the surrendered masses, and all were exempted; then he told the various stockades, “The great army has arrived.”
translations.idiomatic: He enrolled the surrendered men and granted them all amnesty, then sent word to the other camps: “The main army is here.”

sentences.zh: 賊帥句胡僧大驚，斬之，莫能禁，眾執胡僧以降。

translations.literal: The bandit chief Gou Huseng was greatly alarmed and beheaded him; none could stop it; the masses seized Gou Huseng and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel chief Gou Huseng panicked and had the messenger killed, but he could not restrain his men—they seized Gou Huseng and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 韓求知大賊已禽，徇諸壁曰：「敢出者斬！」

translations.literal: Han Qiu, knowing the great bandit had already been captured, proclaimed to the stockades, “Whoever dares come out will be beheaded!”
translations.idiomatic: Han Qiu, now that the great rebel had been taken, announced to the camps, “Anyone who comes out will be executed!”

sentences.zh: 眾罵之，求赴水死，眾鉤出，斬以徇，余柵皆下。

translations.literal: The masses cursed him; Qiu sought death by drowning; the masses hooked him out and beheaded him as a warning; the remaining stockades all submitted.
translations.idiomatic: His followers cursed him. Qiu tried to drown himself, but they dragged him out with hooks, beheaded him as an example, and the rest of the stockades capitulated.

sentences.zh: 仁厚按轡徘徊視賊壘，吏請焚之，仁厚命取財糧，乃縱火，屍賊成都。

translations.literal: Renhou held the reins and paced back and forth viewing the bandit fortifications; officers asked to burn them; Renhou ordered wealth and grain taken first, then set fire; corpses and plunder filled Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Renhou rode slowly about, surveying the rebel strongholds. When his officers asked to burn them, he ordered the wealth and grain removed first, then set them ablaze. Corpses and booty piled up until they seemed to fill Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 仁厚還，天子禦樓勞軍，授仁厚檢校尚書左仆射、眉州刺史。

translations.literal: Renhou returned; the Son of Heaven reviewed troops from the tower and rewarded the army, appointing Renhou Acting Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and prefect of Meizhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Renhou returned, the emperor appeared on the palace tower to review and reward the troops, and appointed him Acting Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and prefect of Meizhou.

sentences.zh: 敬瑄與仁厚謀曰：「秀升未禽，貢輸梗奪，百官乏奉，民不鹽食。

translations.literal: Jingxuan plotted with Renhou, saying, “Xiusheng has not yet been captured; tribute transport is blocked and seized; the hundred officials lack stipends; the people lack salt to eat.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxuan took Renhou aside and said, “Until Xiusheng is captured, tribute cannot get through, the court officials go unpaid, and the people cannot even get salt.

sentences.zh: 公能破賊，當以東川待公。」

translations.literal: If you, sir, can break the bandits, I shall treat you with Eastern Chuan.”
translations.idiomatic: If you can defeat these rebels, I will give you Eastern Chuan.”

sentences.zh: 仁厚許之。

translations.literal: Renhou agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Renhou agreed.

sentences.zh: 詔拜行軍司馬。

translations.literal: An edict appointed him campaigning Vice Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: The court appointed him campaigning vice marshal.

sentences.zh: 仁厚聞賊儲械、子女皆在屯，乃以銳兵瀕江，伐木頹水礙舟道，負岸而陣。

translations.literal: Renhou heard that the bandits stored weapons and that women and children were all in the camp; thereupon with crack troops he lined the riverbank, felled trees to tumble into the water and obstruct the boat channel, and formed battle lines with backs to the shore.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that the rebels had stockpiled arms and that their families were in the camp, Renhou posted elite troops along the river, felled trees into the current to block navigation, and drew up his line with the bank at his back.

sentences.zh: 使遊軍逼賊，久不戰，則夜以千卒持短刀、強弩直薄營，火而噪之。

translations.literal: He sent skirmishers to press the bandits; after long without battle, then at night with a thousand soldiers bearing short swords and powerful crossbows he went straight to storm the camp, set fire, and clamored.
translations.idiomatic: He sent light troops to harry the enemy and, after a long standoff, at night led a thousand men armed with short swords and heavy crossbows in a direct assault on the camp, setting fires and raising a din.

sentences.zh: 秀升率舟兵救火，仁厚遣人鶩沒鑿舟，皆沈，眾懼，多潰。

translations.literal: Xiusheng led boat soldiers to fight the fire; Renhou sent men diving like ducks to bore holes in the boats; all sank; the masses were afraid, and many routed.
translations.idiomatic: Xiusheng led his river force to fight the blaze, but Renhou’s men dived under the boats and scuttled them until every vessel sank. Terrified, most of the rebels broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 秀升斬潰兵，欲脅止之，眾怒，執秀升以降。

translations.literal: Xiusheng beheaded routed soldiers, wishing to coerce and stop them; the masses were angry and seized Xiusheng to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Xiusheng tried to stem the rout by executing fleeing soldiers, but his men, enraged, seized him and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 仁厚問狀，對曰：「天子蒙塵，反者何獨我？」

translations.literal: Renhou questioned him on the facts; he replied, “The Son of Heaven suffers dust on his robes—why am I alone a rebel?”
translations.idiomatic: When Renhou questioned him, he answered, “The Son of Heaven is driven into exile—why should I alone be called a rebel?”

sentences.zh: 仁厚檻車送行在，斬於市。

translations.literal: Renhou sent him in a cangue cart to the traveling court and executed him in the market.
translations.idiomatic: Renhou sent him in a prisoner cart to the emperor’s camp and had him beheaded in the marketplace.

sentences.zh: 東川節度使楊師立初隸神策軍，累遷檢校司空、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: Eastern Chuan military governor Yang Shili at first belonged to the Shence Army and was repeatedly promoted to Acting Minister of Works and equal associate of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Shili, military governor of Eastern Chuan, had begun in the Shence Army and rose to Acting Minister of Works and Joint Manager of Affairs with the Secretariat-Chancellery.

sentences.zh: 聞敬瑄仁厚代己，有望言。

translations.literal: Hearing that Jingxuan and Renhou would replace him, he spoke words of resentment.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard that Chen Jingxuan intended to replace him with Renhou, he spoke bitterly of the injustice.

sentences.zh: 敬瑄諷帝召師立以本官兼尚書右仆射，師立益怒，移檄言敬瑄十罪，殺監軍田繪，屯涪城，遣兵攻綿州，不克。

translations.literal: Jingxuan hinted to the emperor to summon Shili with his original office plus Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs; Shili grew angrier, issued a proclamation listing Jingxuan’s ten crimes, killed supervising commissioner Tian Hui, encamped at Fucheng, and sent troops to attack Mianzhou but did not take it.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxuan persuaded the emperor to recall Shili with his existing rank plus the post of Right Vice Director. Shili grew still angrier, circulated a manifesto listing ten crimes against Chen Jingxuan, killed the supervising commissioner Tian Hui, encamped at Fucheng, and sent troops against Mianzhou without success.

sentences.zh: 又檄劍州刺史姚卓文共攻成都，假卓文為指揮應接使，卓文不應。

translations.literal: He also issued a proclamation to Jianzhou prefect Yao Zhuowen to attack Chengdu jointly, appointing Zhuowen acting coordinating response commander; Zhuowen did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: He also called on Yao Zhuowen, prefect of Jianzhou, to join in an attack on Chengdu and named him coordinating commander, but Zhuowen ignored him.

sentences.zh: 帝乃下詔削官爵。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon issued an edict stripping office and rank.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then issued an edict stripping him of rank and office.

sentences.zh: 敬瑄即表仁厚為東川節度留後，楊茂言為行軍副使，楊棠為諸軍都虞候，率兵三萬討之。

translations.literal: Jingxuan immediately memorialized Renhou as Eastern Chuan military governor designate, Yang Maoyan as campaigning deputy, Yang Tang as commander of all armies, and led thirty thousand troops to attack him.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxuan at once memorialized the court to make Renhou acting governor of Eastern Chuan, Yang Maoyan campaigning deputy, and Yang Tang commander of all forces, and marched thirty thousand men against Shili.

sentences.zh: 師立遣大將張士安、鄭君雄守鹿頭關。

translations.literal: Shili sent great generals Zhang Shi’an and Zheng Junxiong to hold Lutou Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Shili sent his generals Zhang Shi’an and Zheng Junxiong to hold Lutou Pass.

sentences.zh: 仁厚次漢州，前軍戰德陽，師立嬰城，閱四旬，夜出兵擾北柵，仁厚設兩翼而伏，披柵門列炬，賊不敢進，伏發，擊走之。

translations.literal: Renhou halted at Hanzhou; the vanguard fought at Deyang; Shili held the city; after four ten-day periods, at night he sent troops to harass the north camp; Renhou set two wings and an ambush, opened the palisade gate and arrayed torches; the bandits dared not enter; the ambush sprang and struck them away.
translations.idiomatic: Renhou encamped at Hanzhou while his vanguard fought at Deyang. Shili shut himself in the city for forty days, then one night sallied against the northern camp. Renhou deployed wings and an ambush, threw open the palisade gate, and lined torches along the way—the rebels dared not advance, and when the ambush rose they were driven off.

sentences.zh: 楊茂言謂仁厚且敗，引兵走，久乃還。

translations.literal: Yang Maoyan said Renhou was about to be defeated and led troops away; only after a long time did he return.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Maoyan decided Renhou was doomed to lose and withdrew with his troops, returning only after a long delay.

sentences.zh: 明日，會諸將，仁厚曰：「副使當以死報天子。」

translations.literal: The next day, meeting the generals, Renhou said, “The deputy should die to repay the Son of Heaven.”
translations.idiomatic: The next day, at a council of generals, Renhou said, “A deputy who abandons his post ought to die for the Son of Heaven.”

sentences.zh: 斬而徇。

translations.literal: He beheaded him and displayed the head as a warning.
translations.idiomatic: He had him beheaded and displayed the head as a warning.

sentences.zh: 於是士安不敢出，師立自督士，十戰皆北。

translations.literal: Thereupon Shi’an dared not come out; Shili personally supervised the troops; in ten battles all were defeated.
translations.idiomatic: After that Shi’an dared not venture out, and when Shili personally led his men in ten engagements he lost every one.

sentences.zh: 仁厚約城中斬首惡者賞，君雄呼於軍曰：「天子所討，反者耳，吾等何與？」

translations.literal: Renhou promised reward in the city for beheading the chief villains; Junxiong cried to the army, “What the Son of Heaven attacks are rebels only—what have we to do with it?”
translations.idiomatic: Renhou offered rewards within the city for anyone who killed the ringleaders. Junxiong shouted to the troops, “The emperor is punishing rebels—what has that to do with us?”

sentences.zh: 乃與士安嘩而進，以仁厚書示師立曰：「請以死謝眾。」

translations.literal: Thereupon with Shi’an he clamored and advanced, showing Shili Renhou’s letter and saying, “Please die to answer the masses.”
translations.idiomatic: He and Shi’an stormed forward with an uproar, showed Shili Renhou’s letter, and said, “You must die to satisfy the men.”

sentences.zh: 自沈於池死。

translations.literal: He drowned himself in a pool and died.
translations.idiomatic: Shili threw himself into a pool and drowned.

sentences.zh: 君雄悉誅其家，獻首天子。

translations.literal: Junxiong executed his entire family and presented the head to the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Junxiong put Shili’s entire family to death and sent his head to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 仁厚入府，縱系囚，賑貧絕。

translations.literal: Renhou entered the headquarters, released bound prisoners, and relieved the utterly poor.
translations.idiomatic: Renhou entered the governor’s seat, freed the prisoners, and gave relief to the destitute.

sentences.zh: 詔拜劍南東川節度使。

translations.literal: An edict appointed him military governor of Jiannan East Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed him military governor of Jiannan East Circuit.

sentences.zh: 光啟二年，遂據梓州，絕敬瑄。

translations.literal: In the second year of Guangqi he then seized Zizhou and cut off relations with Jingxuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Guangqi he seized Zizhou and broke with Chen Jingxuan.

sentences.zh: 君雄時為遂州刺史，亦陷漢州，攻成都。

translations.literal: Junxiong was then prefect of Suizhou; he also took Hanzhou and attacked Chengdu.
translations.idiomatic: Junxiong, by then prefect of Suizhou, also captured Hanzhou and marched on Chengdu.

sentences.zh: 敬瑄使部將李順之逆戰，君雄死。

translations.literal: Jingxuan sent subordinate general Li Shunzhi to meet him in battle; Junxiong died.
translations.idiomatic: Jingxuan sent his officer Li Shunzhi to meet him in battle, and Junxiong was killed.

sentences.zh: 又發維、茂州羌軍擊仁厚，斬之。

translations.literal: He also mobilized Wei and Mao prefecture Qiang troops to attack Renhou and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: He also raised Qiang forces from Wei and Mao prefectures to attack Renhou and had him beheaded.

sentences.zh: 乾寧中，皆追贈司徒。

translations.literal: In the Qianning era, all were posthumously granted Grand Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: During the Qianning period they were all posthumously made Grand Mentors.

sentences.zh: 趙犨，陳州宛丘人，世為忠武軍牙將。

translations.literal: Zhao Chou, a man of Wanqiu in Chen prefecture; for generations his family served as yamen generals of the Zhongwu Army.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Chou, a native of Wanqiu in Chen prefecture, came from a family that had served for generations as staff generals of the Zhongwu Army.

sentences.zh: 犨資警健，兒弄時好為營陣行列，自號令指顧，群兒無敢亂。

translations.literal: Chou was by nature alert and robust; as a child at play he liked to form camp formations and ranks, himself issuing commands and gestures, and the group of children dared not disorder themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Alert and sturdy by nature, as a boy at play he loved to drill mock camps and battle lines, barking orders and directing the others—and none of the children dared disobey.

sentences.zh: 父叔文見之，曰：「是當大吾門。」

translations.literal: His father Shuwu saw it and said, “This one will greatly honor our house.”
translations.idiomatic: His father Shuwu watched and said, “This boy will bring great honor to our house.”

sentences.zh: 稍長，喜書，學擊劍，善射。

translations.literal: When he grew somewhat older, he loved books, studied swordplay, and was skilled at archery.
translations.idiomatic: As he grew he took to books, trained in swordsmanship, and became an excellent archer.

sentences.zh: 會昌中，從伐潞州，收天井關，又從征蠻，忠武軍功多，遷大校。

translations.literal: In the Huichang era he followed the campaign against Luzhou, took Tianjing Pass, and again followed the expedition against the southern barbarians; the Zhongwu Army had many achievements, and he was promoted to senior commander.
translations.idiomatic: During the Huichang reign he joined the campaign against Luzhou and helped take Tianjing Pass, then served in the southern expeditions. The Zhongwu Army won many honors, and he rose to senior commander.

sentences.zh: 黃巢入長安，所在盜興，陳人詣節度府，請犨為刺史，表於朝，授之。

translations.literal: When Huang Chao entered Chang’an, bandits rose everywhere; the people of Chen went to the circuit headquarters requesting Chou as prefect, memorialized the court, and he was appointed.
translations.idiomatic: When Huang Chao entered Chang’an, brigands sprang up everywhere. The people of Chen went to the circuit seat and asked that Chou be made prefect; the court was petitioned, and the appointment was granted.

sentences.zh: 既視事，會官屬計曰：「巢若不死長安，必東出關，陳其沖也。」

translations.literal: Once he took office, he gathered officials and staff to plan, saying, “If Chao does not die in Chang’an, he must surely go east out through the pass—Chen is its choke point.”
translations.idiomatic: As soon as he took office he called his staff together and said, “If Huang Chao does not die in Chang’an, he will surely march east through the passes—and Chen stands in his path.”

sentences.zh: 乃培城疏塹，實倉庫，峙槁薪，為守計。

translations.literal: Thereupon he heightened the walls, dredged the moat, filled the granaries, piled firewood, and made plans for defense.
translations.idiomatic: He raised the walls, cleared the moat, filled the granaries, stacked fuel, and prepared for a siege.

sentences.zh: 民有貲者悉內之，繕甲兵，募悍勇，悉補子弟領兵。

translations.literal: Wealthy commoners all contributed inward; he repaired armor and weapons, recruited fierce and brave men, and all supplemented them with family sons and younger brothers to lead troops.
translations.idiomatic: Wealthy citizens poured in their resources; he repaired arms and armor, recruited the toughest fighters, and placed his own kin in command of every unit.

sentences.zh: 巢敗，果東奔。

translations.literal: Chao was defeated and indeed fled east.
translations.idiomatic: When Huang Chao was defeated he did indeed flee eastward.

sentences.zh: 賊將孟楷以萬人寇項，犨擊禽之。

translations.literal: The bandit general Meng Kai with ten thousand men raided Xiang; Chou attacked and captured him.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel general Meng Kai invaded Xiang with ten thousand men, but Chou attacked and took him prisoner.

sentences.zh: 僖宗嘉其功，遷累檢校司空。

translations.literal: Emperor Xizong praised his achievement and repeatedly promoted him to Acting Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xizong praised his achievement and promoted him step by step to Acting Minister of Works.

sentences.zh: 巢聞楷死，驚且怒，悉軍據溵水，與秦宗權合兵數十萬，繚長壕五周，百道攻之。

translations.literal: Chao heard that Kai was dead, was shocked and angry, mustered the entire army and held the Yin River, joined Qin Zongquan’s troops to several hundred thousand, encircled with long trenches five rounds deep, and attacked along a hundred routes.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Chao, hearing that Kai was dead, was shocked and furious. He massed his entire army on the Yin River, joined Qin Zongquan for a force of hundreds of thousands, dug five rings of trenches around the city, and assaulted it from every side.

sentences.zh: 州人大恐，犨令曰：「士貴建功立名節，今雖眾寡不敵，男子當死地求生，徒懼無益也。

translations.literal: The people of the prefecture were greatly afraid; Chou ordered, saying, “Gentlemen value establishing achievement and preserving integrity and reputation; though now few cannot match many, a man should seek life in a place of certain death—mere fear is of no use.
translations.idiomatic: The people of the prefecture were terrified. Chou proclaimed, “A true soldier wins fame by deeds of honor. Though we are outnumbered, a man should fight where death is certain if he hopes to live—fear alone will save no one.

sentences.zh: 且死國，不愈生為賊乎？

translations.literal: Moreover, to die for the state—is it not better than living as a bandit?
translations.idiomatic: Is it not better to die for one’s country than to live on as a rebel’s slave?

sentences.zh: 吾家食陳祿，誓破賊以保陳，異議者斬！」

translations.literal: My family eats Chen’s salary; I swear to break the bandits to preserve Chen—whoever disagrees will be beheaded!”
translations.idiomatic: My family has eaten Chen’s grain. I swear to break these rebels and save the city—and anyone who disagrees will be beheaded!”

sentences.zh: 眾聽命。

translations.literal: The masses obeyed the command.
translations.idiomatic: The people obeyed.

sentences.zh: 引銳士出戰，屢破賊。

translations.literal: He led crack troops out to battle and repeatedly defeated the bandits.
translations.idiomatic: He led his best troops out again and again and repeatedly routed the rebels.

sentences.zh: 巢益怒，將必屠之，乃起八仙營於州左，僭象宮闕，列百官曹署，儲糧為持久計。

translations.literal: Chao grew angrier and was determined to massacre them; thereupon he raised the Eight Immortals Camp east of the prefecture, presumptuously imitating palace gates and towers, arrayed the hundred officials’ bureaus, and stored grain for a prolonged plan.
translations.idiomatic: Huang Chao, growing still angrier, resolved to slaughter the city to the last man. He built an “Eight Immortals” camp east of the walls, mock palaces and halls, offices for a full bureaucracy, and stockpiled grain for a long siege.

sentences.zh: 宗權輸鎧仗軍須，賊益張。

translations.literal: Zongquan supplied armor, weapons, and military necessities; the bandits grew still more arrogant.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Zongquan sent armor, arms, and supplies, and the rebels grew bolder still.

sentences.zh: 犨小大數百戰，勝負相當，故人心固，乃間道乞師於朱全忠。

translations.literal: Chou fought several hundred battles large and small; victories and defeats were roughly equal; therefore hearts were firm; then by a secret path he begged troops from Zhu Quanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Chou fought hundreds of engagements, great and small, with roughly even success, which kept morale firm. Meanwhile he sent secret envoys to Zhu Quanzhong begging for reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 未幾，汴軍至，壁西北，陳人思奮，犨引兵急擊賊，破之。

translations.literal: Before long the Bian troops arrived and encamped northwest; the people of Chen thought to exert themselves; Chou led troops in urgent attack on the bandits and broke them.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Bian army arrived and camped to the northwest. The people of Chen took heart, and Chou led a fierce assault that broke the rebel lines.

sentences.zh: 圍凡三百日而解。

translations.literal: The siege in all lasted three hundred days before it was lifted.
translations.idiomatic: The siege lasted three hundred days in all before it was lifted.

sentences.zh: 中和五年，擢彰義軍節度使。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhonghe he was promoted to military governor of the Zhangyi Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Zhonghe he was made military governor of the Zhangyi Army.

sentences.zh: 巢雖敗，宗權始熾，略地數千里，屠二十餘州，唯陳賴犨獨完，以功檢校司徒，加泰寧、浙西兩節度，皆在陳並領之。

translations.literal: Though Chao was defeated, Zongquan at first grew fierce, ravaged territory for several thousand li, and slaughtered more than twenty prefectures; only Chen, relying on Chou, remained intact alone; for his achievement he was made Acting Grand Mentor, and Taining and Zhexi circuits were added—both administered from Chen and held concurrently.
translations.idiomatic: Though Huang Chao was beaten, Qin Zongquan now rose to power, seizing territory for thousands of li and massacring people in more than twenty prefectures. Chen alone, thanks to Chou, stood intact. For this he was made Acting Grand Mentor and given the Taining and Zhexi circuits as well—all governed from Chen in his own hands.

sentences.zh: 龍紀初，進同中書門下平章事、忠武軍節度，仍治陳州，流亡踵還。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Longji he was advanced to equal associate of the Secretariat-Chancellery and Zhongwu Army military governor, still governing Chen prefecture; exiles returned in succession.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Longji era he was made Grand Councillor and military governor of the Zhongwu Army, still administering Chen. Refugees streamed home.

sentences.zh: 與弟昶至友愛，後將老，悉以軍事付之，乃卒，贈太尉。

translations.literal: With his younger brother Chang he was extremely affectionate; later, as he grew old, he entrusted all military affairs to him; then he died and was posthumously granted Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: He and his younger brother Chang were deeply devoted to one another. In his later years, as age overtook him, he handed all military affairs to Chang, then died and was posthumously made Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 犨悉忠力以孤城抗賊，巢卒敗亡。

translations.literal: Chou exhausted loyalty and strength to hold a lone city against the bandits; Chao ultimately was defeated and perished.
translations.idiomatic: Chou poured all his loyalty and strength into holding a single city against the rebels, and Huang Chao was ultimately destroyed.

sentences.zh: 然附全忠，亦賴其力復振，故委輸調發助全忠，常先它鎮雲。

translations.literal: Yet he attached himself to Quanzhong and also relied on his strength to revive; therefore tribute transport and dispatch assisted Quanzhong, often ahead of other circuits, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he also leaned on Zhu Quanzhong and owed his recovery to Zhu’s power, so his supplies and levies went to aid Zhu first—ahead of every other circuit, men said.

sentences.zh: 昶，字大東，神采軒異，而內沈厚，有法度。

translations.literal: Chang, style name Dadong, had a spirited bearing lofty and unusual, yet inwardly was deep and substantial, with standards of law.
translations.idiomatic: Chang, whose style was Dadong, had a striking, commanding presence, yet inwardly he was calm and steady and governed by strict discipline.

sentences.zh: 破孟楷功多。

translations.literal: In defeating Meng Kai his achievement was great.
translations.idiomatic: He won great distinction in the capture of Meng Kai.

sentences.zh: 巢之圍，昶夜掫師，疲而寢，如有神相之者。

translations.literal: During Chao’s siege, Chang at night patrolled the army; weary, he slept—as if a spirit aided him.
translations.idiomatic: During Huang Chao’s siege he led the night patrol. Though exhausted, he would fall asleep on watch as if some spirit watched over him.

sentences.zh: 犁曙決戰，士爭奮死鬥，禽賊酋數人，斬級千餘。

translations.literal: At daybreak he fought a decisive battle; soldiers vied to exert themselves and die fighting; he captured several bandit chieftains and beheaded more than a thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn he fought a decisive battle. His men strove to the death, capturing several rebel chiefs and taking more than a thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 犨領泰寧，以昶為州刺史、檢校尚書右仆射。

translations.literal: Chou held Taining and appointed Chang prefect of the prefecture and Acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When Chou held Taining he appointed Chang prefect of the circuit and Acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 當時，方鎮言忠壯吏治，舉言犨、昶。

translations.literal: At the time, when circuits spoke of loyal robustness in civil governance, all cited Chou and Chang.
translations.idiomatic: In those days, whenever the regional governors spoke of loyal, forceful administration, they named Chou and Chang.

sentences.zh: 犨之老，乃授留後，遷忠武節度使，亦留陳。

translations.literal: When Chou grew old, he then entrusted the post of military governor designate; Chang was transferred to Zhongwu Army military governor and also remained at Chen.
translations.idiomatic: In his old age Chou made him his designated successor, then transferred the Zhongwu governorship to him while both remained at Chen.

sentences.zh: 進檢校司徒。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Acting Grand Mentor.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Acting Grand Mentor.

sentences.zh: 劭勸農桑，於人有恩惠。

translations.literal: Chang encouraged agriculture and sericulture and showed kindness to people.
translations.idiomatic: He encouraged farming and sericulture and treated the people with kindness.

sentences.zh: 加同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: He was added as equal associate of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 乾寧二年卒，年五十三，贈太尉。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qianning he died, age fifty-three, and was posthumously granted Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second year of Qianning at the age of fifty-three and was posthumously made Grand Commandant.

sentences.zh: 犨子珝，字有節。

translations.literal: Chou’s son Pin, style name Youjie.
translations.idiomatic: Chou’s son Pin, whose style was Youjie.

sentences.zh: 雄毅喜書，善騎射。

translations.literal: Bold and steadfast, he loved books and was skilled at riding and archery.
translations.idiomatic: Bold and resolute, he loved learning and was skilled in horsemanship and archery.

sentences.zh: 巢之難，激勵麾下，約皆死。

translations.literal: During Chao’s calamity, he exhorted and encouraged those under his command, pledging that all would die.
translations.idiomatic: During Huang Chao’s siege he roused his men and bound them by oath to fight to the death.

sentences.zh: 以先冢邇賊，畏見殘齮，即夜縋死士取柩以入。

translations.literal: Because his ancestors’ tombs were near the bandits, fearing they would be seen mutilated and gnawed, that very night he lowered dare-to-die men by rope to bring the coffins inside.
translations.idiomatic: His family tombs lay close to the enemy lines, and he feared the dead would be desecrated. That night he sent volunteers down the walls on ropes to bring the coffins into the city.

sentences.zh: 庫有巨弩，機牙壞，不能張，珝以意調治，激矢至五百步，人馬皆洞，賊畏不敢逼。

translations.literal: In the arsenal was a great crossbow whose trigger mechanism was broken and could not be drawn; Pin by intuition adjusted and repaired it; when the bolt was released it reached five hundred paces, men and horses were all pierced through, and the bandits feared and dared not press close.
translations.idiomatic: The arsenal held a great crossbow whose mechanism was broken and could not be drawn. Pin repaired it by instinct; when fired, its bolts carried five hundred paces and pierced men and horses clean through. The rebels feared it and dared not press the attack.

sentences.zh: 以勞檢校尚書右仆射，遙領處州刺史。

translations.literal: For his labors he was made Acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and held concurrently the distant post of prefect of Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was made Acting Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and given nominal appointment as prefect of Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 昶帥忠武，珝遷行軍司馬。

translations.literal: Chang commanded the Zhongwu Army; Pin was transferred to campaigning Vice Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: When Chang took command of the Zhongwu Army, Pin was made campaigning vice marshal.

sentences.zh: 昶之喪，知忠武留後，政簡濟，上下安之。

translations.literal: At Chang’s mourning, he acted as Zhongwu military governor designate; his governance was simple and effective, and superiors and subordinates were at peace.
translations.idiomatic: After Chang’s death he served as acting governor of the Zhongwu Army. His rule was plain and effective, and officers and men alike were content.

sentences.zh: 全忠表為忠武軍節度使。

translations.literal: Quanzhong memorialized the court to make him Zhongwu Army military governor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong petitioned the court to appoint him military governor of the Zhongwu Army.

sentences.zh: 陳土惡善圮，珝疊甓表墉，遂無患。

translations.literal: Chen’s soil was poor and prone to collapse; Pin stacked bricks facing the wall surface, and thereafter there was no trouble.
translations.idiomatic: Chen’s poor soil made the walls prone to collapse; Pin faced them with layers of brick, and the problem ceased.

sentences.zh: 三加檢校太保。

translations.literal: Three times he was added Acting Grand Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: He was three times promoted to Acting Grand Guardian.

sentences.zh: 光化三年，同中書門下平章事，進兼侍中，封天水郡公。

translations.literal: In the third year of Guanghua he became equal associate of the Secretariat-Chancellery, was advanced to concurrent Palace Attendant, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Tianshui commandery.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Guanghua he was made Grand Councillor, promoted to concurrent Palace Attendant, and enfeoffed as Duke of Tianshui.

sentences.zh: 按鄧艾故跡，決翟王渠溉稻以利農。

translations.literal: Following Deng Ai’s old traces, he opened the Zhaiwang Canal to irrigate rice fields for the benefit of agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: Following the route of Deng Ai’s old canal, he opened the Zhaiwang Channel to irrigate the rice fields and benefit the farmers.

sentences.zh: 一家三節度，相繼二十餘年，陳人宜之。

translations.literal: One family held three military governorships in succession for more than twenty years; the people of Chen found it fitting.
translations.idiomatic: One family held three governorships in succession for more than twenty years, and the people of Chen were well content.

sentences.zh: 天復初，韓建帥忠武，以珝知同州節度留後。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianfu, Han Jian commanded the Zhongwu Army and had Xu act as Tongzhou circuit military governor designate.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Tianfu era Han Jian took over the Zhongwu Army and appointed Xu acting governor of Tongzhou circuit.

sentences.zh: 昭宗還長安，詔入朝，賜號「迎鑾功臣」。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhaozong returned to Chang’an, an edict summoned him to court and granted the title “Meritorious Minister Who Welcomed the Imperial Carriage.”
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhaozong returned to Chang’an, Xu was summoned to court and given the title “Meritorious Minister Who Welcomed the Imperial Carriage.”

sentences.zh: 以檢校太傅為右金吾衛上將軍，從東遷。

translations.literal: As Acting Grand Tutor he served as senior general of the Right Golden Crow Guard and followed the eastward move.
translations.idiomatic: As Acting Grand Tutor he became senior general of the Right Golden Crow Guard and accompanied the court’s move east.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，以疾免。

translations.literal: After more than a year, he was relieved because of illness.
translations.idiomatic: After a year he resigned on grounds of illness.

sentences.zh: 卒，年五十五，贈侍中，陳人為罷市。

translations.literal: He died, age fifty-five, and was posthumously granted Palace Attendant; the people of Chen closed the markets in mourning.
translations.idiomatic: He died at fifty-five and was posthumously made Palace Attendant. The people of Chen shut down the markets in mourning.

sentences.zh: 田頵，字德臣，廬州合肥人。

translations.literal: Tian Yun, style name Dechen, was a man of Hefei in Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Yun, whose style was Dechen, came from Hefei in Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 略通書傳，沈果有大志。

translations.literal: He had some mastery of books and classics; deep and resolute, he had great ambition.
translations.idiomatic: He had some learning in the classics, and was deep, resolute, and ambitious.

sentences.zh: 與楊行密同里，約為兄弟。

translations.literal: He was of the same village as Yang Xingmi and pledged brotherhood.
translations.idiomatic: He and Yang Xingmi were from the same town and swore brotherhood.

sentences.zh: 應州募屯邊，遷主將。

translations.literal: When the prefecture recruited for garrison duty on the frontier, he was promoted to chief commander.
translations.idiomatic: When the circuit recruited frontier garrison troops, he rose to chief commander.

sentences.zh: 行密據廬州，頵謀為多。

translations.literal: When Xingmi held Luzhou, Yun’s stratagems were many.
translations.idiomatic: After Xingmi seized Luzhou, Yun supplied most of his stratagems.

sentences.zh: 攻趙锽於宣州，锽出東溪，乘暴流以逸，阻水解甲，謂追騎不能及。

translations.literal: Attacking Zhao Huang at Xuanzhou, Huang went out through East Creek, rode the raging current to escape, reached the obstructing water and removed his armor, thinking pursuing cavalry could not catch up.
translations.idiomatic: In the attack on Zhao Huang at Xuanzhou, Huang fled down East Creek on the swollen current, reached a broad stretch of water, and doffed his armor, believing the pursuers could not catch him.

sentences.zh: 頵乘輕舠追之，锽驚，遂見禽。

translations.literal: Yun pursued in a light boat; Huang was alarmed and was thereupon captured.
translations.idiomatic: Yun gave chase in a light boat. Huang panicked and was taken.

sentences.zh: 行密表頵為馬步軍都虞候。

translations.literal: Xingmi memorialized the court to make Yun commander of all horse and foot armies.
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi petitioned the court to appoint Yun commander of all cavalry and infantry.

sentences.zh: 沙陀叛將安仁義奔淮南，行密大喜，屬以騎兵，使在頵右，兩人名冠軍中，共攻常州，殺刺史杜棱。

translations.literal: The Shatuo rebel general An Renyi fled to Huainan; Xingmi was greatly pleased, entrusted him with cavalry, and placed him at Yun’s right; the two men’s fame topped the army; together they attacked Changzhou and killed prefect Du Ling.
translations.idiomatic: The Shatuo defector An Renyi fled to Huainan. Xingmi was delighted, gave him command of the cavalry, and paired him with Yun—the two finest commanders in the army. Together they took Changzhou and killed the prefect Du Ling.

sentences.zh: 錢鏐方屯潤州，一夕潰。

translations.literal: Qian Liu was just then encamped at Runzhou; in one night his force collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Liu had been encamped at Runzhou, but his army collapsed overnight.

sentences.zh: 會孫儒南略，頵等屯丹陽，儒火揚州，壁廣德，頵破其屯。

translations.literal: When Sun Ru marched south, Yun and others encamped at Danyang; Ru burned Yangzhou and fortified Guangde; Yun broke his camp.
translations.idiomatic: When Sun Ru marched south, Yun and the others held Danyang. Ru burned Yangzhou and fortified Guangde, but Yun smashed his camp.

sentences.zh: 與戰，頵走，行密怒，奪其兵。

translations.literal: In battle Yun fled; Xingmi was angry and stripped him of his troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the fighting Yun was routed. Xingmi, furious, stripped him of command.

sentences.zh: 或諫行密曰：「強敵傅壘，不用頵，非計也。」

translations.literal: Someone admonished Xingmi, saying, “A strong foe presses the ramparts—not to use Yun is no plan.”
translations.idiomatic: Someone urged Xingmi, “With a powerful enemy at the walls, refusing to use Yun is poor strategy.”

sentences.zh: 行密復將頵。

translations.literal: Xingmi again put Yun in command.
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi restored Yun to command.

sentences.zh: 儒詒書仁義通好，以疑行密，行密待益厚，署行軍副使，卒用此二人功禽儒。

translations.literal: Ru sent a deceitful letter to Renyi proposing friendship to sow doubt in Xingmi; Xingmi treated him still more generously, appointed him campaigning deputy, and in the end by these two men’s merit captured Ru.
translations.idiomatic: Ru sent a feigned letter of friendship to Renyi to sow suspicion against Xingmi, but Xingmi treated Renyi all the more generously and made him campaigning deputy. In the end these two men’s efforts brought about Ru’s capture.

sentences.zh: 乃表仁義為潤州刺史，頵寧國軍節度使。

translations.literal: Thereupon he memorialized Renyi as prefect of Runzhou and Yun as military governor of the Ningguo Army.
translations.idiomatic: He then petitioned the court to make Renyi prefect of Runzhou and Yun military governor of the Ningguo Army.

sentences.zh: 累遷檢校太保、同中書門下平章事。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Acting Grand Guardian and equal associate of the Secretariat-Chancellery.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted in succession to Acting Grand Guardian and Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 仁義至檢校太保。

translations.literal: Renyi reached Acting Grand Guardian.
translations.idiomatic: Renyi rose to Acting Grand Guardian.

sentences.zh: 頵已平馮弘鐸，至揚州謝行密。

translations.literal: Yun had already pacified Feng Hongduo and came to Yangzhou to thank Xingmi.
translations.idiomatic: After pacifying Feng Hongduo, Yun came to Yangzhou to pay his respects to Xingmi.

sentences.zh: 左右求貲不已，獄吏亦有請，頵怒曰：「吏覬吾入獄邪！」

translations.literal: Those at his side asked for bribes without cease; prison clerks also made requests; Yun angrily said, “Do clerks covet my entering prison?”
translations.idiomatic: His attendants kept demanding gifts, and even the prison clerks asked for bribes. Yun raged, “Do you clerks expect me in your jail?”

sentences.zh: 又求池、歙為屬州，行密不許，頵始怨。

translations.literal: He also asked that Chi and She be made subordinate prefectures; Xingmi did not permit it; Yun began to resent.
translations.idiomatic: He also demanded that Chi and She be made his subordinate prefectures. Xingmi refused, and Yun’s resentment began.

sentences.zh: 將還，指府門曰：「吾不復入此。」

translations.literal: About to return, he pointed at the headquarters gate and said, “I shall not enter here again.”
translations.idiomatic: As he was leaving he pointed at the headquarters gate and said, “I will never set foot in here again.”

sentences.zh: 是時，錢镠部將徐綰叛，镠入杭州逐綰，綰屯靈隱山迎頵。

translations.literal: At this time Qian Liu’s subordinate general Xu Wan rebelled; Liu entered Hangzhou to drive Wan out; Wan encamped at Lingyin Mountain to welcome Yun.
translations.idiomatic: About then Qian Liu’s officer Xu Wan rebelled. Liu entered Hangzhou to drive him out, and Wan encamped on Lingyin Mountain to welcome Yun.

sentences.zh: 頵遣客何曉見镠曰：「王宜東保會稽，無為虛屠士眾也。」

translations.literal: Yun sent his guest He Xiao to see Liu, saying, “Your Highness ought to guard Kuaiji in the east—do not vainly slaughter soldiers and masses.”
translations.idiomatic: Yun sent his envoy He Xiao to Qian Liu with the message, “Your Highness should withdraw east to Kuaiji—do not waste your men in a pointless slaughter.”

sentences.zh: 镠曰：「軍中小叛常然，公為人長，何助逆耶？」

translations.literal: Liu said, “Small rebellions in the army are common; you, sir, are an elder—why aid the traitor?”
translations.idiomatic: Liu replied, “Petty mutinies in the ranks are nothing new. You are a man of standing—why aid a rebel?”

sentences.zh: 頵攻北門，镠登城與語，射中麾下。

translations.literal: Yun attacked the north gate; Liu ascended the wall to speak with him and shot one of Yun’s followers.
translations.idiomatic: Yun attacked the north gate. Liu mounted the wall to parley with him and shot one of Yun’s officers.

sentences.zh: 頵築壘絕往來道，镠患之，出金幣十輿，募能奪地者。

translations.literal: Yun built ramparts cutting off the thoroughfare; Liu was troubled by it and offered gold and coins in ten cartloads to recruit anyone who could seize back the ground.
translations.idiomatic: Yun built fortifications that cut off the roads. Troubled, Liu offered ten cartloads of gold and cash to anyone who could break through.

sentences.zh: 陳璋以死士三百，免胄馳擊，奪其地，镠授璋衢州刺史。

translations.literal: Chen Zhang with three hundred dare-to-die men, bareheaded, charged at a gallop and seized back the ground; Liu appointed Zhang prefect of Quzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Zhang led three hundred dare-to-die men in a bareheaded charge, retook the ground, and Liu made him prefect of Quzhou.

sentences.zh: 頵攻城未能克，將濟江絕西陵，為镠將所卻，圍益急。

translations.literal: Yun could not take the city by assault; he was about to cross the river and cut off Xiling but was repelled by Liu’s generals; the siege grew still tighter.
translations.idiomatic: Yun failed to take the city by assault and tried to cross the river to cut off Xiling, but Liu’s generals drove him back and tightened the siege.

sentences.zh: 先是，行密欲女镠子，镠急，乃遣元迎女，且告行密曰：「頵得誌，為患必大，請以子為質，願召還頵。」

translations.literal: Earlier, Xingmi had wished to marry a daughter to Liu’s son; Liu was urgent and thereupon sent Yuan Guan to welcome the girl, and also told Xingmi, “If Yun succeeds, the harm will surely be great—please take my son as hostage and recall Yun.”
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Xingmi had sought a marriage alliance with Liu’s son. In desperation Liu sent Yuan Guan to fetch the bride and told Xingmi, “If Yun succeeds the damage will be grave. Take my son as hostage and recall Yun.”

sentences.zh: 行密使人謂頵曰：「不還，我遣人代守宣州。」

translations.literal: Xingmi sent someone to tell Yun, “If you do not return, I shall send someone to replace you in holding Xuanzhou.”
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi sent word to Yun: “If you do not return, I will send someone else to hold Xuanzhou.”

sentences.zh: 頵不從。

translations.literal: Yun did not obey.
translations.idiomatic: Yun refused.

sentences.zh: 镠輸錢二百萬緡犒軍，頵又請镠子元瓘出質，乃與綰引兵還。

translations.literal: Liu supplied two million strings of cash to reward the army; Yun also asked that Liu’s son Yuan Guan come out as hostage; thereupon with Wan he led troops back.
translations.idiomatic: Liu paid two million strings of cash to reward the army. Yun also demanded that Liu’s son Yuan Guan be left as hostage. Only then did he withdraw with Xu Wan.

sentences.zh: 然內怨行密與镠，因移書曰：「侯王守方以奉天子，譬百川不朝於海，雖狂奔澶漫，終為涸土，不若順流無窮也。

translations.literal: Yet inwardly he resented Xingmi and Liu; therefore he sent a letter saying, “Marquises and kings guard their regions to serve the Son of Heaven—it is like the hundred streams not paying court to the sea; though they rush wildly and spread vast, in the end they become dry earth; it is not like following the current without end.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he nursed resentment against Xingmi and Liu and wrote: “Princes hold their domains in service to the Son of Heaven. It is like the hundred streams not paying court to the sea—however wildly they rush and spread, they end as dry earth; better to follow the current without end.

sentences.zh: 東南揚為大，刀布金玉積如阜，願公上天子常賦，頵請悉儲峙，單車以從。」

translations.literal: In the southeast Yang is greatest; knives, cloth, gold, and jade pile like mounds; I wish that you, sir, go up to the Son of Heaven with regular tribute—Yun asks to store and pile all of it and follow with a single cart.”
translations.idiomatic: The southeast’s greatest power is Yangzhou, where gold and goods pile like hills. Go yourself to present the emperor’s regular tribute—I will store everything and follow you with a single cart.”

sentences.zh: 行密答曰：「貢賦繇汴而達，適足資敵爾。」

translations.literal: Xingmi replied, “Tribute and levies reach the court by way of Bian— that would only supply the enemy.”
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi answered, “Tribute must pass through Bianzhou—that would only arm our enemy.”

sentences.zh: 於是頵絕行密，大募兵。

translations.literal: Thereupon Yun broke with Xingmi and recruited troops on a large scale.
translations.idiomatic: Yun then broke with Xingmi and raised a great army.

sentences.zh: 李神福白行密：「頵必叛，宜先圖之。」

translations.literal: Li Shenfu informed Xingmi, “Yun will surely rebel—you ought to plot against him first.”
translations.idiomatic: Li Shenfu warned Xingmi, “Yun will certainly rebel. You should strike first.”

sentences.zh: 行密曰：「頵有大功，而反狀未明，殺之，諸將不為用。」

translations.literal: Xingmi said, “Yun has great achievements, and the signs of rebellion are not yet clear—if I kill him, the generals will not serve me.”
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi said, “Yun has rendered great service, and his treason is not yet proven. If I kill him, the other generals will not follow me.”

sentences.zh: 頵遣其佐杜荀鶴至汴通好，全忠喜，屯宿州須變。

translations.literal: Yun sent his aide Du Xunhe to Bian to open friendly relations; Quanzhong was pleased and encamped at Suzhou awaiting developments.
translations.idiomatic: Yun sent his aide Du Xunhe to Bian to treat with Zhu Quanzhong, who was delighted and encamped at Suzhou to await events.

sentences.zh: 行密以康儒在頵所，故授廬州刺史以間之。

translations.literal: Xingmi, because Kang Ru was at Yun’s place, therefore appointed him prefect of Luzhou to sow division.
translations.idiomatic: Because Kang Ru was with Yun, Xingmi appointed him prefect of Luzhou to drive a wedge between them.

sentences.zh: 頵怒，族其家，儒曰：「公不用吾謀，死無地矣。」

translations.literal: Yun was angry and exterminated his clan; Ru said, “My lord, you did not use my plan—I shall die with nowhere to be buried.”
translations.idiomatic: Yun, enraged, executed Kang Ru’s entire family. Ru said, “You would not heed my counsel—now I have nowhere to die but here.”

sentences.zh: 頵與安仁義連和攻升州，劫刺史李神福妻息厚養之。

translations.literal: Yun joined with An Renyi to attack Shengzhou and seized Prefect Li Shenfu’s wife and children, treating them generously.
translations.idiomatic: Yun allied with An Renyi to attack Shengzhou and seized Li Shenfu’s wife and children, keeping them in comfortable custody.

sentences.zh: 神福方與劉存攻鄂州，行密召之。

translations.literal: Shenfu was just then with Liu Cun attacking Ezhou; Xingmi summoned him.
translations.idiomatic: Shenfu was besieging Ezhou with Liu Cun when Xingmi recalled him.

sentences.zh: 神福謂諸將曰：「頵反，此心腹疾，宜速攻之。」

translations.literal: Shenfu told the generals, “Yun has rebelled—this is a disease of the heart and belly; we ought to attack quickly.”
translations.idiomatic: Shenfu told his officers, “Yun has rebelled. This is a mortal threat—we must attack at once.”

sentences.zh: 頵遣李臯詒書神福曰：「公家在此，茍從我，當分地以王。」

translations.literal: Yun sent Li Gao with a deceitful letter to Shenfu, saying, “Your family is here—if you will only follow me, I shall divide territory and make you a king.”
translations.idiomatic: Yun sent Li Gao with a letter offering, “Your family is in my hands. Join me and I will divide the realm and make you a king.”

sentences.zh: 答曰：「吾以一卒從吳王，任上將，終不以妻子易意。」

translations.literal: He replied, “I followed the King of Wu from a single soldier’s rank to command as a senior general—I will never change my mind for wife and children.”
translations.idiomatic: Shenfu answered, “I followed the Prince of Wu from the ranks to high command. I will not change my loyalty for wife and children.”

sentences.zh: 乃斬臯，破頵兵於曷山。

translations.literal: Thereupon he beheaded Gao and defeated Yun’s troops at Mount He.
translations.idiomatic: He beheaded Gao and routed Yun’s army at Mount He.

sentences.zh: 始，頵將王壇等以舟師躡神福後，至吉陽磯，不戰。

translations.literal: At first Yun’s generals Wang Tan and others with a river force followed on Shenfu’s heels; reaching Jiyang Ford, they did not fight.
translations.idiomatic: Yun’s generals Wang Tan and others pursued with the fleet as far as Jiyang Ford but did not give battle.

sentences.zh: 會日暮，壇掩神福軍半濟，神福反舟順流急擊，大破之，因縱火，士多死。

translations.literal: It happened to be dusk; Tan struck Shenfu’s army half across the ford; Shenfu turned his boats and with the current rushed to attack, greatly defeating them; thereupon he set fire, and many soldiers died.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk Tan struck while Shenfu’s men were half across the river. Shenfu wheeled his boats downstream and counterattacked, routing them and setting fire to the fleet—many drowned or burned.

sentences.zh: 明日，壇復戰，敗於皖口，頵乃自將來戰。

translations.literal: The next day Tan fought again and was defeated at Wankou; Yun thereupon personally led troops to battle.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Tan fought again and was beaten at Wankou. Yun then took the field in person.

sentences.zh: 神福曰：「賊棄城而來，此天亡也。」

translations.literal: Shenfu said, “The bandits abandoned their city to come—this is Heaven’s destruction of them.”
translations.idiomatic: Shenfu said, “The enemy has abandoned his city to fight us here—Heaven means to destroy him.”

sentences.zh: 乃瀕水堅壁不出，請行密以兵塞頵走道。

translations.literal: Thereupon along the water he fortified firmly and did not come out, asking Xingmi to send troops to block Yun’s escape route.
translations.idiomatic: He fortified his camp along the river and refused battle, while asking Xingmi to block Yun’s line of retreat.

sentences.zh: 仁義焚東塘戰艦，夜攻常州，不克，轉戰至夾岡，立二幟，解甲而息，追兵莫敢向。

translations.literal: Renyi burned the warships at Dongtang, attacked Changzhou by night without taking it, fought on to Jiagang, set up two banners, removed armor and rested, and pursuing troops dared not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Renyi burned his warships at Dongtang, attacked Changzhou by night without success, and fought his way to Jiagang. There he raised two banners, laid aside his armor, and rested—his pursuers dared not approach.

sentences.zh: 頵陳舟蕪湖。

translations.literal: Yun arrayed boats at Wuhu.
translations.idiomatic: Yun stationed his fleet at Wuhu.

sentences.zh: 行密遣將王茂章攻潤州。

translations.literal: Xingmi sent the general Wang Maozhang to attack Runzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi sent Wang Maozhang to attack Runzhou.

sentences.zh: 仁義以善射冠軍中，當時稱朱瑾槊，米誌誠弩，皆為第一。

translations.literal: Renyi for skill in archery topped the army; at the time they called Zhu Jin’s spear and Mi Zhicheng’s crossbow each first in their kind.
translations.idiomatic: Renyi was the finest archer in the army. Men said Zhu Jin’s spear and Mi Zhicheng’s crossbow were each unmatched in their day.

sentences.zh: 仁義常曰：「誌誠弩十，不當瑾槊之一；

translations.literal: Renyi often said, “Ten of Zhicheng’s crossbow shots are not worth one of Jin’s spear thrusts;
translations.idiomatic: Renyi used to say, “Ten of Mi Zhicheng’s bolts are not worth one thrust of Zhu Jin’s spear;

sentences.zh: 瑾槊十，不當吾弓之一。」

translations.literal: ten of Jin’s spear thrusts are not worth one of my bow shots.”
translations.idiomatic: and ten of Zhu Jin’s spear thrusts are not worth one shot from my bow.”

sentences.zh: 人以為然。

translations.literal: People thought it so.
translations.idiomatic: People believed him.

sentences.zh: 又其治軍嚴，善得士心。

translations.literal: Moreover, his governance of the army was strict, and he was good at winning soldiers’ hearts.
translations.idiomatic: He also ran a strict camp and knew how to win his men’s loyalty.

sentences.zh: 戰卒數百，濠梁不毀，開門鬥，先告所當中，然後射之。

translations.literal: With several hundred battle soldiers, the moat and bridge were not destroyed; he opened the gate to fight, first announcing whom he would hit, then shooting.
translations.idiomatic: With only a few hundred men at arms he left the moat bridge intact, opened the gate to fight, called out whom he would hit, and then shot—and hit.

sentences.zh: 茂章等不敢與確。

translations.literal: Maozhang and the others dared not engage him decisively.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Maozhang and the others dared not close with him.

sentences.zh: 行密遣使謂曰：「吾不忘公功，能自歸，當復為行軍副使，但不可處兵。」

translations.literal: Xingmi sent an envoy telling him, “I do not forget your achievements; if you can return of yourself, you shall again be campaigning deputy—but you may not hold troops.”
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi sent word: “I have not forgotten your service. Surrender and I will restore you as campaigning deputy—but you may not keep an army.”

sentences.zh: 仁義欲降，其子固諫，乃止。

translations.literal: Renyi wished to surrender; his son firmly admonished him, and he stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Renyi was ready to yield, but his son dissuaded him and he held back.

sentences.zh: 行密召其將臺濛泣語曰：「人嘗告頵必反，我不忍負人，頵果負我。

translations.literal: Xingmi summoned his general Tai Meng and, weeping, said, “People once told me Yun would surely rebel; I could not bear to wrong a man—Yun has indeed wronged me.
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi summoned his general Tai Meng and said through tears, “Men warned me Yun would rebel, but I could not bear to wrong him—and he has wronged me.

sentences.zh: 吾思為將者非公莫可。」

translations.literal: I think for a commander there is no one but you, sir.”
translations.idiomatic: I can think of no commander but you for this.”

sentences.zh: 濛頓首謝，率騎度江，為陣以行。

translations.literal: Meng bowed his head in thanks, led cavalry across the river, and advanced in battle formation.
translations.idiomatic: Meng kowtowed, led his cavalry across the river, and advanced in battle order.

sentences.zh: 士笑其怯，濛曰：「頵宿將多謀，備之何害？」

translations.literal: The soldiers laughed at his timidity; Meng said, “Yun is a veteran general with many stratagems—what harm in being prepared?”
translations.idiomatic: His men laughed at his caution. Meng said, “Yun is a seasoned commander and full of stratagems—what harm is there in being ready?”

sentences.zh: 與王壇等戰廣德，濛以行密書遺壇諸將，皆再拜氣奪。

translations.literal: Fighting Wang Tan and others at Guangde, Meng sent Xingmi’s letter to Tan’s generals; all bowed twice and their spirit was seized.
translations.idiomatic: At Guangde he fought Wang Tan and sent Xingmi’s letter to Tan’s officers. They all bowed low, their spirit broken.

sentences.zh: 濛麾兵擊之，壇走。

translations.literal: Meng waved his troops to attack; Tan fled.
translations.idiomatic: Meng ordered the attack and Tan fled.

sentences.zh: 神福既以不戰困頵，頵紿言母病，還至蕪湖。

translations.literal: Shenfu had already wearied Yun by not fighting; Yun falsely said his mother was ill and returned to Wuhu.
translations.idiomatic: Shenfu had worn Yun down by refusing battle. Yun pretended his mother was ill and withdrew to Wuhu.

sentences.zh: 聞壇敗，留精兵二萬屬郭行琮，身走城。

translations.literal: Hearing Tan was defeated, he left twenty thousand elite troops under Guo Xingcong and himself fled to the city.
translations.idiomatic: When he heard Tan was beaten, he left twenty thousand picked troops with Guo Xingcong and raced for the city himself.

sentences.zh: 濛之行，為狹營小舍，覘者以為才容二千人，頵輕之，不復召兵。

translations.literal: On Meng’s march he made narrow camps and small huts; observers thought they could hold only two thousand men; Yun belittled him and did not summon more troops.
translations.idiomatic: On the march Meng pitched narrow camps and small shelters. Scouts thought he had barely two thousand men. Yun despised him and did not call up reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 與戰黃池，矢石始交而濛遁，兵爭逐北，遇伏，頵大敗，召蕪湖兵，不得入。

translations.literal: They fought at Huangchi; arrows and stones had just begun to clash when Meng fled; soldiers vied to pursue the defeated; they met an ambush; Yun was greatly defeated; he called the Wuhu troops but could not enter.
translations.idiomatic: At Huangchi, as arrows and stones first flew, Meng feigned retreat. Yun’s men rushed in pursuit, ran into an ambush, and were routed. Yun called for his Wuhu troops but they could not reach him.

sentences.zh: 行琮及壇皆歸行密，頵恚，自料死士數百，號「爪牙都」，身薄戰。

translations.literal: Xingcong and Tan both returned to Xingmi; Yun was resentful, personally selected several hundred dare-to-die men, called them the “Fang and Claw Division,” and pressed into battle himself.
translations.idiomatic: Xingcong and Tan both went over to Xingmi. Furious, Yun picked several hundred dare-to-die men, called them the “Fang and Claw Corps,” and led the charge himself.

sentences.zh: 濛退軍示弱，士超隍，濛殊死戰，軍潰。

translations.literal: Meng withdrew his army to show weakness; soldiers crossed the moat; Meng fought to the death; the army collapsed.
translations.idiomatic: Meng drew back as if beaten. Yun’s men crossed the moat; Meng turned and fought desperately. Yun’s army broke.

sentences.zh: 頵奔城，橋陷，為亂兵所殺，年四十六。

translations.literal: Yun fled toward the city; the bridge collapsed; he was killed by disorderly troops, age forty-six.
translations.idiomatic: Yun fled for the city, but the bridge gave way and he was killed in the rout at the age of forty-six.

sentences.zh: 其下猶鬥，示頵首，乃潰。

translations.literal: His subordinates still fought; when Yun’s head was shown, only then did they collapse.
translations.idiomatic: His men fought on until Yun’s head was displayed—then they scattered.

sentences.zh: 頵始以元瓘歸，戰不勝，輒欲殺之，頵母護免。

translations.literal: At first Yun had returned Yuan Guan; when battles were not won he would want to kill him; Yun’s mother protected and spared him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuan Guan was first sent back as a hostage, Yun would threaten to kill him after every defeat, but Yun’s mother protected him.

sentences.zh: 及镠與行密合，頵曰：「今日不勝，必殺元瓘。」

translations.literal: When Liu and Xingmi joined forces, Yun said, “If we do not win today, I shall surely kill Yuan Guan.”
translations.idiomatic: When Qian Liu and Xingmi joined forces, Yun said, “If we do not win today, I will kill Yuan Guan.”

sentences.zh: 已而頵死，傳首至淮南，行密泣下，葬以庶人禮，亦葬康儒，還元瓘於杭。

translations.literal: Before long Yun died; his head was sent to Huainan; Xingmi wept; he buried him with commoner rites, also buried Kang Ru, and returned Yuan Guan to Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: But Yun died first. When his head reached Huainan, Xingmi wept, buried him with commoner rites, buried Kang Ru as well, and sent Yuan Guan back to Hangzhou.

sentences.zh: 頵善為治，資寬厚，通利商賈，民愛之。

translations.literal: Yun was good at governance, by nature generous and mild, facilitated merchants’ profit, and the people loved him.
translations.idiomatic: Yun was an able administrator—generous by nature, friendly to trade, and beloved by the people.

sentences.zh: 善遇士，若楊夔、康軿、夏侯淑、殷文圭、王希羽等皆為上客。

translations.literal: He treated scholars well; such men as Yang Kui, Kang Kai, Xiahou Shu, Yin Wengui, and Wang Xiyu were all honored guests.
translations.idiomatic: He treated scholars generously. Yang Kui, Kang Kai, Xiahou Shu, Yin Wengui, Wang Xiyu, and others were all honored as chief guests.

sentences.zh: 文圭有美名，全忠、镠交辟不應。

translations.literal: Wengui had a fine reputation; Quanzhong and Liu repeatedly summoned him by turns, but he did not respond.
translations.idiomatic: Wengui enjoyed a fine reputation. Both Zhu Quanzhong and Qian Liu repeatedly invited him, but he refused them all.

sentences.zh: 頵置田宅，迎其母，以甥事之，故文圭為盡力。

translations.literal: Yun set up fields and a residence, welcomed his mother, and treated him as a sister’s son; therefore Wengui exerted himself to the utmost for him.
translations.idiomatic: Yun gave him land and a house, welcomed his mother, and treated him as a sister’s son—so Wengui served him with all his strength.

sentences.zh: 夔知頵不足亢行密，著《溺賦》以戒，頵不用。

translations.literal: Kui knew Yun was not sufficient to resist Xingmi; he composed “The Drowning Rhapsody” as a warning, but Yun did not use it.
translations.idiomatic: Kui saw that Yun could not stand against Xingmi and wrote “The Rhapsody of Drowning” as a warning, but Yun ignored it.

sentences.zh: 行密使王茂章穴地取潤州，安仁義以家屬保城樓，兵不敢登。

translations.literal: Xingmi had Wang Maozhang tunnel underground to take Runzhou; Renyi placed his family on the gate tower as protection, and troops dared not ascend.
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi had Wang Maozhang tunnel into Runzhou. Renyi put his family on the gate tower as a shield, and the attackers dared not climb up.

sentences.zh: 召李德誠曰：「汝可以委命。」

translations.literal: He summoned Li Decheng and said, “You may entrust your life to me.”
translations.idiomatic: He summoned Li Decheng and said, “You may trust me with your life.”

sentences.zh: 乃抵弓矢就縛，父子斬揚州市。

translations.literal: Thereupon he set down bow and arrows and submitted to binding; father and son were beheaded in the Yangzhou marketplace.
translations.idiomatic: Then he laid down his bow, submitted to bonds, and he and his son were beheaded in Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 濛，字頂雲，亦合肥人。

translations.literal: Meng, style name Dingyun, was also a man of Hefei.
translations.idiomatic: Meng, whose style was Dingyun, was also from Hefei.

sentences.zh: 頵破，行密表為檢校太保、宣州觀察使。

translations.literal: When Yun was defeated, Xingmi memorialized the court to make him Acting Grand Guardian and Xuanzhou observation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: After Yun’s defeat, Xingmi petitioned the court to make Meng Acting Grand Guardian and commissioner of Xuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 天祐初卒。

translations.literal: He died at the beginning of Tianyou.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the beginning of the Tianyou era.

sentences.zh: 朱延壽者，廬州舒城人。

translations.literal: Zhu Yanshou was a man of Shucheng in Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Yanshou came from Shucheng in Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 事行密，破秦彥、畢師鐸、趙锽、孫儒功居多。

translations.literal: He served Xingmi; in defeating Qin Yan, Bi Shiduo, Zhao Huang, and Sun Ru his achievements were foremost.
translations.idiomatic: He served Yang Xingmi and won the greatest share of credit in defeating Qin Yan, Bi Shiduo, Zhao Huang, and Sun Ru.

sentences.zh: 行密欲以寬恕結人心，而延壽敢殺。

translations.literal: Xingmi wished to bind people’s hearts through leniency, but Yanshou dared to kill.
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi wanted to win loyalty through mercy, but Yanshou was ruthless in killing.

sentences.zh: 時揚州多盜，捕得者，行密輒賜所盜遣之，戒曰：「勿使延壽知。」

translations.literal: At the time Yangzhou had many bandits; when any were caught, Xingmi would give them what they had stolen and send them away, warning, “Do not let Yanshou know.”
translations.idiomatic: Yangzhou had many thieves in those days. When one was caught, Xingmi would return the stolen goods and release him with the warning, “Do not let Yanshou know.”

sentences.zh: 已而陰許延壽殺之。

translations.literal: Before long he secretly permitted Yanshou to kill them.
translations.idiomatic: Then he secretly allowed Yanshou to execute them.

sentences.zh: 初，壽州刺史高彥溫舉州入朱全忠，行密襲之，諸將憚城堅不可拔，延壽鼓之，拔其城即表為淮南節度副使。

translations.literal: Earlier, Shouzhou prefect Gao Yanwen had surrendered the entire prefecture to Zhu Quanzhong; Xingmi raided it; the generals feared the city’s stout walls could not be taken; Yanshou roused them, captured the city, and was immediately memorialized as Huainan military governor deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Gao Yanwen of Shouzhou had surrendered his prefecture to Zhu Quanzhong. When Xingmi attacked, the other generals feared the strong walls could not be taken. Yanshou rallied the men, took the city, and was at once made deputy military governor of Huainan.

sentences.zh: 全忠猶屯壽春，延壽以新軍出，每旗五伍為列，遣李厚以十旗擊西偏，不勝，將斬之，厚請益五旗，殊死戰，全忠引去。

translations.literal: Quanzhong was still encamped at Shouchun; Yanshou led out the new army, each banner in columns of five squads of five; he sent Li Hou with ten banners to strike the west flank; they did not win; he was about to behead Hou; Hou asked for five more banners, fought to the death, and Quanzhong withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Quanzhong still held Shouchun. Yanshou led out fresh troops in tight five-man squads under each banner and sent Li Hou with ten banners against the western flank. When Hou was beaten, Yanshou was about to execute him—but Hou begged for five more banners, fought desperately, and drove Zhu Quanzhong away.

sentences.zh: 於是取黃、蘄、光三州，以功遷壽州團練使。

translations.literal: Thereupon he took the three prefectures Huang, Qi, and Guang, and for his achievement was transferred to Shouzhou defense commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He then seized Huang, Qi, and Guang prefectures and was made defense commissioner of Shouzhou for his merit.

sentences.zh: 昭宗在鳳翔，詔延壽圍蔡以披全忠勢，擢奉國軍節度使。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhaozong was at Fengxiang, an edict ordered Yanshou to besiege Cai to break Quanzhong’s momentum, and he was promoted to military governor of the Fengguo Army.
translations.idiomatic: While Emperor Zhaozong was at Fengxiang, Yanshou was ordered to besiege Cai and relieve Zhu Quanzhong’s pressure, and was promoted to military governor of the Fengguo Army.

sentences.zh: 全忠兵每至，延壽開門不設備，而不敢逼也。

translations.literal: Whenever Quanzhong’s troops arrived, Yanshou opened the gates without setting defenses, yet they dared not press him.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever Zhu Quanzhong’s troops came up, Yanshou would open his gates without preparing defenses—yet they never dared press him.

sentences.zh: 延壽用軍常以寡鬥眾，敗還者盡斬之。

translations.literal: Yanshou in using troops often fought many with few; those who returned defeated were all beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: Yanshou often fought larger forces with smaller ones, and beheaded every man who came back defeated.

sentences.zh: 田頵之附全忠，延壽陰約曰：「公有所為，我願執鞭。」

translations.literal: When Tian Yun attached himself to Quanzhong, Yanshou secretly agreed, saying, “Whatever you undertake, sir, I wish to hold the whip.”
translations.idiomatic: When Tian Yun sided with Zhu Quanzhong, Yanshou secretly pledged, “Whatever you plan, sir, I am ready to serve at your side.”

sentences.zh: 頵喜，二人謀絕行密。

translations.literal: Yun was pleased; the two men plotted to cut off Xingmi.
translations.idiomatic: Yun rejoiced, and the two plotted to destroy Yang Xingmi.

sentences.zh: 行密憂甚，紿病目，行觸柱僵。

translations.literal: Xingmi was deeply worried; he feigned eye disease, walked and struck a pillar and fell stiff.
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi was deeply worried. He pretended to be going blind, stumbled against a pillar, and collapsed.

sentences.zh: 妻，延壽姊也，掖之。

translations.literal: His wife was Yanshou’s elder sister; she supported him.
translations.idiomatic: His wife—Yanshou’s elder sister—helped him up.

sentences.zh: 行密泣曰：「吾喪明，諸子幼，得舅代我，無憂矣。」

translations.literal: Xingmi wept and said, “I have lost my sight; my sons are young—if I can have my uncle replace me, there will be no worry.”
translations.idiomatic: Xingmi wept and said, “I am going blind, and my sons are still young. With my uncle to take my place, I need fear nothing.”

sentences.zh: 遣辯士召之，延壽疑，不肯赴。

translations.literal: He sent a persuasive speaker to summon him; Yanshou was suspicious and would not come.
translations.idiomatic: He sent an eloquent envoy to summon him, but Yanshou was suspicious and would not come.

sentences.zh: 姊遣婢報故，延壽疾走揚州，拜未訖，士禽殺之，而廢其妻。

translations.literal: His sister sent a maid to report the truth; Yanshou raced to Yangzhou; before his bow was finished, soldiers seized and killed him, and his wife was deposed.
translations.idiomatic: His sister sent a maid with the truth. Yanshou raced to Yangzhou, but before he could finish his bow soldiers seized and killed him, and his wife was cast aside.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：全忠，唐之盜也，行密誌梟其元而後已。

translations.literal: The commentator says: Quanzhong was a robber of Tang; Xingmi resolved to display his head on a pole before he would stop.
translations.idiomatic: The commentator says: Zhu Quanzhong was a robber of the Tang. Yang Xingmi swore he would not rest until Zhu’s head was spiked for all to see.

sentences.zh: 田頵使出軍賦而助之，此其謀責難而絕之，非忠於唐也。

translations.literal: Tian Yun sent out army levies to aid him—this was his plan to press for accountability and cut him off; it was not loyalty to Tang.
translations.idiomatic: When Tian Yun sent troops and supplies to aid Zhu, his aim was to hold Zhu accountable and then break with him—not loyalty to the Tang.

sentences.zh: 棄所附而覬尊大，亦已妄矣。

translations.literal: To abandon whom he had attached himself to and covet supreme greatness was already delusion.
translations.idiomatic: To abandon his patron and reach for supremacy on his own was already folly.

sentences.zh: 孔子稱孟公綽為趙、魏老則優，不可以為滕、薛大夫。

translations.literal: Confucius said that Meng Gongchuo as steward for Zhao and Wei would be excellent, but could not serve as grand officer of Teng and Xue.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said Meng Gongchuo would excel as steward to the great houses of Zhao and Wei, but could not serve as minister to small states like Teng and Xue.

sentences.zh: 如仁厚、田、朱，材不足為吳、蜀之老，可與事天子哉！

translations.literal: Men like Renhou, Tian, and Zhu—their talent was insufficient to be stewards for Wu and Shu; how could they serve the Son of Heaven!
translations.idiomatic: Men like Renhou, Tian, and Zhu lacked the talent even to be stewards in the kingdoms of Wu and Shu—how could they hope to serve the Son of Heaven!
